title: Trench Warfare Adventure
welcome_lead: Climb into a WW1 trench on the Western Front. Mud, rats, machine guns — and going 'over the top'. 🪖
meta_desc: Trenches Adventure — a KS3 walkthrough of trench warfare on the WW1 Western Front.

concepts.def: Line of trenches across France and Belgium
Long ditch dug for soldiers to fight from
Climbing out of a trench to attack
Foot disease from cold, wet conditions

walkthroughs.body_html:
After the first months of fighting in 1914, both sides 'dug in'.

The Western Front became a line of trenches over 400 miles long, from the Belgian coast to the Swiss border.

Between the two armies lay No Man's Land, criss-crossed with barbed wire and shell holes. 🌧️

A trench had a fire step to stand on, dugouts to sleep in, and zig-zags to limit blast damage.

Daily routine: 'stand-to' at dawn, repairs, sentry duty, sleep, food, letters home. Rats stole rations; lice lived in uniforms.

In cold mud feet rotted — called trench foot. Endless shelling left many soldiers with shell shock.

To attack, soldiers had to climb out and run across No Man's Land — 'going over the top'.

They faced machine guns, barbed wire and artillery. Gains were tiny — sometimes a field, for thousands of lives.

On the first day of the Somme (1 July 1916), Britain lost about 57,000 men in a single day. Soldiers wrote bitter poems about what they saw. 📝
